newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds open weaker in very light activity.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds open weaker in very light activity.

text.p: Canadian bonds opened slightly weaker on Monday, mirroring losses by U.S. Treasuries, with activity very light amid a lack of signifcant economic data, analysts said.

"Activity is extremely light. This is the quietest morning we've had in a long, long time, so I don't think we can gauge this little bit of a sell-off in a very important way," said Hank Cunningham, director of fixed income with First Marathon Securities Ltd.
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond fell C$0.38 to C$118.59 to yield 6.571 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond fell 7/32 to yield 6.55 percent. The spread between the bonds was two basis points, unchanged from the close of trading on Friday.
Both Canadian and U.S. bond markets opened slightly weaker amid moderate profit-taking. Activity was light in both countries with traders focused on economic data out later in the week.
Key Canadian economic reports out this week include the consumer price index for June out on Thursday. Merchandise and wholesale trade data for May will be released on Friday.

"The key event in the next two weeks is going to be (Fed chairman Alan Greenspan's) Humphrey-Hawkins testimony. I think the market is going to tread water a lot until then. His remarks may set the tone for the next several months," said Cunningham. Greenspan will testify on July 22.
In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond fell C$0.29 to C$109.16 to yield 6.004 percent. The U.S. 30-year bond fell 5/32 to yield 6.25 percent.
The negative spread between the two benchmark bonds moved to 25 basis points from 24 basis points at the close of trading on Friday.
The three-month cash T-bill yielded 3.15 percent against its U.S. equivalent which yielded 5.13 percent.
